title: Integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation reveal the antifungal and anti-inflammatory mechanisms of Camellia oleifera seed extracts against oral thrush.
authors: Zhang, Xiaohua; Zeng, Xiaochuan; Zheng, Ming; Qiu, Xiongwen; Zhang, Fan; Shi, Qiaorui
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用网络药理学和分子对接探讨油茶籽提取物抗口腔念珠菌病的抗真菌抗炎机制，虽含分子对接但对象为化合物-蛋白（STAT3），非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Oral thrush, primarily caused by Candida albicans, is often accompanied by inflammation and pain. Due to rising resistance and side effects of current antifungal treatments, safer and more effective alternatives are needed. This study investigates the antifungal mechanisms of Camellia oleifera seed extracts against oral thrush using network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vitro validation. UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS identified chemical components in the extracts, selecting those meeting Lipinski's Rule of Five. Oral thrush-related targets were retrieved from public databases, and a compound-target network was built to identify key targets. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks, GO, and KEGG analyses were conducted. Molecular docking assessed interactions between active compounds and core targets. Antifungal efficacy and cytotoxicity were evaluated in vitro. Twenty-three active compounds were identified. Tea saponin showed favorable docking scores to STAT3, a key intracellular mediator of IL-6-driven inflammatory signaling, suggesting potential modulation of the IL-6/STAT3 axis. The extracts inhibited Candida albicans growth and biofilm formation in vitro; however, cytotoxicity toward human gingival fibroblasts was observed at concentrations lower than those required for antifungal efficacy, resulting in a limited therapeutic index. Camellia oleifera seed extracts exhibit antifungal and anti-inflammatory activity against oral thrush in vitro, but their therapeutic window appears narrow under the conditions tested. These findings highlight the potential of the extracts as lead candidates for topical or formulation-optimized antifungal applications, while emphasizing the need for further optimization and in vivo safety evaluation.
abstract_zh: 口腔鹅口疮主要由白色念珠菌（Candida albicans）引起，常伴有炎症和疼痛。由于现有抗真菌治疗的耐药性及副作用日益增加，亟需更安全、更有效的替代方案。本研究通过网络药理学、分子对接（molecular docking）及体外验证，探讨油茶（Camellia oleifera）种子提取物对口腔鹅口疮的抗真菌机制。采用UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS鉴定提取物中的化学成分，并筛选符合利平斯基五规则（Lipinski's Rule of Five）的化合物。从公共数据库获取口腔鹅口疮相关靶点，构建化合物-靶点网络以识别关键靶点。进行了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络、GO及KEGG分析。分子对接评估了活性化合物与核心靶点之间的相互作用。体外评价了抗真菌功效及细胞毒性。共鉴定出23种活性化合物。茶皂素（tea saponin）与STAT3（IL-6驱动炎症信号传导的关键细胞内介质）显示出良好的对接得分，提示其可能调节IL-6/STAT3轴。提取物在体外抑制了白色念珠菌的生长及生物膜形成；然而，在低于抗真菌有效浓度时，提取物对人牙龈成纤维细胞表现出细胞毒性，导致治疗指数有限。油茶种子提取物在体外对口腔鹅口疮具有抗真菌及抗炎活性，但在所测试条件下其治疗窗口较窄。这些发现凸显了提取物作为局部或制剂优化抗真菌应用的先导候选物的潜力，同时强调需进一步优化及体内安全性评估。
